name: ActionButton
description: One button that handles the permission check, an optional confirmation, the pending state and a result message for an action. It does not fetch data, show toasts, cache or route: you pass the function that does the work.

children.description: Button label. Name the action, such as Delete user.

onAction.description: The work. May be async; its resolved value goes to onSuccess and a throw or rejection goes to onError.

permission.description: What the person may do: allow (default), disabled (shown, focusable, says why) or hidden (renders nothing). Use { state: "disabled", reason } to explain. The server must check again.

confirm.tsType: { title: string; description?: string; confirmLabel?: string; cancelLabel?: string; confirmText?: string }
confirm.description: Ask first. Opens an alert dialog (danger tone when the variant is danger); the confirm button runs onAction. confirmText makes the person type a word before it works.

icon.description: Icon shown before the label. Decorative, so the label must say what the button does.

successMessage.description: Announced politely to screen readers when the action succeeds. Show your own toast in onSuccess if you also want it on screen.

errorMessage.description: Announced politely to screen readers when the action fails.

onSuccess.description: Called with the resolved value when the action succeeds.

onError.description: Called with the error when the action throws or rejects.

onStateChange.description: Called when the state moves between idle, pending, success and error.

keyboard: With confirm, Enter or Space opens the dialog; Esc cancels it
requirements: A disabled action with a reason stays focusable (aria-disabled) and its reason is linked with aria-describedby and a tooltip
A disabled action with no reason is a normal disabled button
While pending a second press is ignored and the button is marked busy
The result message is announced through a polite status region, not a focus move
screenReader: Announced as a button with its label
Disabled with a reason: announced as dimmed, then the reason is read as its description
Pending: announced as unavailable and busy
Success or failure: the message is spoken politely after the action settles

use_when: A button that calls your API or mutation and needs permission, confirmation, pending and a result
Delete, archive, send and approve actions in tables and forms
avoid_when: Submitting a Form: use the form's submit button
Reading or caching data: that stays with your data layer
anti_patterns: Relying on the disabled state as security: the backend must check again
Hiding the reason when an action is disabled
